elements.quote: A systematic review with metaanalysis of prevalence was conducted in October 2023
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review with meta-analysis.

elements.quote: The aim of this study was to find out the prevalence and factors that favoured the development of depression in nursing students during the COVID-19 pandemic.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective explicitly.

elements.quote: Quantitative primary studies using anonymous scales and surveys to assess the prevalence of depression in nursing students in the last 3 years were included.
elements.reason: Inclusion criteria are summarized but exclusion criteria are not mentioned in the abstract.

elements.quote: conducted in October 2023, using Pubmed, CINAHL and Scopus as the data sources used for the search
elements.reason: Information sources (PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus) and the search date (October 2023) are reported.
The abstract does not describe any risk of bias assessment method (MMAT is only described in the main text).

elements.quote: A systematic review with metaanalysis of prevalence was conducted
elements.reason: The abstract specifies that results were synthesized via a meta-analysis of prevalence.

elements.quote: The final set of articles was N = 12. ... The total sample of students in the meta-analysis was n = 4,479
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies and total participants, plus characteristics (young, female students, concerns, coping mechanisms).

elements.quote: Studies show a high prevalence of depression among young university students with figures above 50%.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcome (depression prevalence).

elements.quote: a prevalence value of 32% (CI95% 22%-42%)
elements.reason: The meta-analytic summary estimate and its 95% confidence interval are reported.

elements.quote: a meta-analysis of prevalence
elements.reason: The review is a meta-analysis of prevalence without comparative groups, so no direction of effect between groups applies.
The abstract does not mention limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias or heterogeneity.

elements.quote: In conclusion, students, especially female students, are at high risk of depression due to social isolation. In addition, coping techniques were inadequate and future strategies to prevent this situation should be considered.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an interpretation of the results and implications for future prevention strategies.
The abstract does not state any funding source for the review (funding appears only in the front matter).
The abstract provides no registration name or registration number.

elements.quote: The pandemic meant a change in academic approach. This had an impact on the mental health of students, leading to, among other problems, depressive disorders.
elements.reason: Only a brief contextual background is provided in the abstract (pandemic-related academic changes affecting student mental health). No retrieved text describes the current state of knowledge (e.g., existing prevalence evidence) or important uncertainties, and no dedicated Introduction/rationale section is present in the evidence.

elements.quote: The aim of this study was to find out the prevalence and factors that favoured the development of depression in nursing students during the COVID-19 pandemic.
elements.reason: The aim is clearly stated and the preceding context implies a need (pandemic impact on student mental health), but the importance and need for the review are not explicitly argued, and no full rationale/Introduction section is available in the retrieved evidence.

The retrieved evidence contains no mention or citation of existing or similar systematic reviews on this topic, and the review is not framed as an update or replication of a previous review; based on the available evidence the condition does not appear to be triggered.

elements.quote: Asystematic review of the scientific literature and a meta-analysis of prevalence was carried out for this article.
elements.reason: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of prevalence, not a review of intervention effects, so no intervention mechanism of action needs to be described.

elements.quote: Asystematic review of the scientific literature and a meta-analysis of prevalence was carried out for this article.
elements.reason: The review addresses prevalence of depression (an observational question), not a complex intervention or delivery context, so a logic model requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: Therefore, the aim of this study was to analyse the factors that favoured the development of depression in university nursing students during the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as to estimate the prevalence of this disorder in this university group.
elements.reason: The objectives are explicitly stated in the Introduction (and echoed in the abstract), but they are not formulated using a recognized question-formulation framework (e.g., PICO, PCC, SPIDER); the review is of prevalence/factors, and no structured framework is reported.

elements.quote: A systematic review with metaanalysis of prevalence was conducted in October 2023
elements.reason: This is a review of prevalence and associated factors, not of intervention effects, so planned comparisons in PICO format do not apply.

elements.quote: Inclusion criteria: primary quantitative studies; ... the design had to be quantitative; without geographical restriction by country; the study population of the articles was focused on nursing students suffering from depression at the time of COVID-19
elements.reason: Eligibility criteria specify population (nursing students with depression during COVID-19), study designs (quantitative, primary studies), and setting (no geographical restriction).

elements.quote: the articles that were included were in English and Spanish; ... they had to have been published in the last 3 years, i.e. between 2020 and 2023
elements.reason: Report characteristics are specified: language (English and Spanish) and publication year range (2020-2023).
The manuscript does not distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.
No groups for the synthesis are specified; the meta-analysis only estimates overall prevalence of depression without defining subgroups or comparisons linked to review objectives.
Restrictions such as language limits, publication window, and exclusion of doctoral theses are stated but no rationales are provided for these restrictions.

elements.quote: The search was conducted in October 2023.
elements.reason: A single search date (October 2023) is reported, applying to the databases searched (PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus).

elements.quote: The electronic databases used for the bibliographic search were: Pubmed, CINAHL and Scopus
elements.reason: Database names are reported, but no search interfaces/platforms or coverage dates are specified.
No registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories were reported as searched; only bibliographic databases and reference checking were used.
No websites or search engines were reported as searched.
No organisations or manufacturers were contacted to identify studies.
No individuals were contacted to identify studies.

elements.quote: finally, reviewing the references included in the selected articles
elements.reason: Reference lists of the selected (included) articles were examined, specifying the type of reference lists consulted.

elements.quote: by performing a reverse search analysing the bibliography of these 11 articles, 3 more were retrieved
elements.reason: Backward citation searching is reported (seed reports = the 11 included articles), but no citation index/platform or search date for this step is specified.
No journals or conference proceedings were directly consulted as sources.

elements.quote: The electronic databases used for the bibliographic search were: Pubmed, CINAHL and Scopus... The following search equation was used: '(undergraduate nurses OR nursing students) AND depression AND (COVID19 OR Sars-CoV-2)'.
elements.reason: A single search equation is reported, but it is not shown as actually run per database (no database-specific syntax, fields, or MeSH terms per source), so the full search strategies for each database are not completely reported.

elements.quote: they had to have been published in the last 3 years, i.e. between 2020 and 2023 which is when the COVID-19 pandemic took place
elements.reason: Limits (language, publication years 2020-2023, study design) are described in the eligibility criteria, but their application as search filters and their justification are only partially linked to the eligibility criteria; it is unclear whether they were applied within the database searches.

elements.quote: The search was conducted in October 2023.

elements.quote: Arandom-effects meta-analysis was performed using the meta-analysis package of Statsdirect software to estimate the prevalence of depression in nursing students. To estimate the prevalence, the total sample size and the sample with depression of each study were used.

No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes and their rationale are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure are described.

elements.quote: Once the aforementioned search criteria had been applied, the bibliography was selected in the following steps: reading the title, reading the abstract, reading the full text and finally, reviewing the references included in the selected articles.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the study selection process (inclusion/exclusion criteria and sequential screening steps, corroborated by the Fig 1 flow diagram in text_9), but it does not describe processes for deciding which studies were eligible for each synthesis, such as tabulating study characteristics against planned synthesis groups. elements.quote: To estimate the prevalence, the total sample size and the sample with depression of each study were used.

elements.quote: The review and selection of articles was carried out by two reviewers. In case of disagreement, a third reviewer would act.

elements.quote: In the initial search of the databases described above, 320 articles were selected. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, a screening was performed and 88 published papers were selected. No duplicate articles were found. After reading the title and abstract, 37 articles were selected
elements.reason: Numbers identified (320, with per-database counts in Fig 1: Scopus 107, Pubmed 180, CINAHL 33), duplicates (none), screened, and excluded after title/abstract screening (n=232 in Fig 1) are all reported.

elements.quote: After reading the title and abstract, 37 articles were selected and after a full reading, 11 were left.
elements.reason: Numbers assessed for full-text eligibility are reported (88 full text, 17 selected in Fig 1), but exclusions at full-text stage are not broken down with counts and primary reasons for each exclusion; the flow diagram lists general exclusion criteria without full-text exclusion reasons/counts.

elements.quote: Finally, by performing a reverse search analysing the bibliography of these 11 articles, 3 more were retrieved, leaving a final sample of n = 14 articles.
elements.reason: The number of included studies (14) is explicitly reported, consistent with the flow diagram's final 'Selected documents n=14'.
No ongoing studies or associated reports are mentioned anywhere in the retrieved evidence; this element does not apply.
This is a new systematic review, not an update of a previous review; no previous review is referenced.
No automation tools were used in the screening process; all screening was done by human reviewers, so distinguishing human vs automated exclusions does not apply.

elements.quote: Documents excluded after reading the title and abstract n=232. Documents excluded from each database: Scopus (n=55), Pubmed (n=159) and CINAHL (n=18). Exclusion criteria: Bibliographic reviews, meta-analyzes, clinical cases, duplicates and cases not related to the subject of study.
elements.reason: The PRISMA flow diagram (Fig 1, chunk text_9) reports numbers of excluded records and general exclusion criteria, but no specific citations of individual excluded studies with study-specific reasons for exclusion are provided.

elements.quote: Studies critical reading was performed following the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) guidelines [34], so that any potential biases and limitations could be discussed.

elements.quote: Studies critical reading was performed following the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) guidelines [34]
elements.reason: The review used the MMAT, a study-level appraisal tool that does not generate outcome-specific risk-of-bias judgements, so outcome-specific RoB display alongside results does not apply.

elements.quote: Alsolais et al. [45], 2021 (Saudi Arabia). ... 1057 nursing students. ... 9% had some degree of depression, anxiety and stress. ... 56.7% of respondents were categorized as in the normal range, 8.3% were severe, and 11.0% were very severe.
elements.reason: Table 1 reports sample sizes and prevalence/results for each study, but group-level summary statistics are incomplete (e.g., Alomari et al. has '-' for prevalence) and full descriptive statistics per group are not systematically provided for every study and outcome.

elements.quote: There was no statistically significant difference between the groups in terms of depression (t = 0.854, p = 0.960), anxiety (t = 1.563, p = 0.123) and stress (t = 1.128, p = 0.264) before laughter therapy.
